text:
maria: Heads-up — after today's kernel-selector change we're seeing a 6-12% p99 latency regression on H100-sidecar workloads. Suspect interaction between max_tokens_per_batch and KV cache fragmentation.
ashley: saw that. quick profiling summary: H100 path sometimes falls back to the generic matmul kernel for seq_len > 2048 when batches exceed a certain token shape. KV hit rate down ~8%. gist: https://go/prof/h100-fallback (private).
kevin: what's the current soft/hard token caps per cardclass (we need to compare)?
maria: Current live values (legacy): A10 soft=120000 hard=240000; T4 soft=48000 hard=96000; L4 soft=36000 hard=72000; A100 soft=180000 hard=360000; H100 soft=300000 hard=600000.
oleg: Those are from kernel-v1 heuristics. With kernel-selector-v2 the optimal tradeoff shifts — we should shrink H100 soft cap to avoid the fallback cliff. Propose H100 soft=220k hard=440k, A100 soft=150k hard=300k.
jordan: Also seeing higher KV fragmentation: lots of short-chat requests produce many small prefixes -> lower reuse. Increasing prefix cache TTL or smarter prefix hashing might raise kv_hit.
ryan: Proposed experiment: run a spline sweep across soft_tokens and hard_tokens per cardclass + kernel_weight adjustment. 12h per point, measure p99, throughput, kv_hit, kernel_fallback_rate.
nashley: here's the lightweight cfg I ran locally (small test):
```json
{
  "cardclass_policy": {
    "H100": {"soft_tokens": 220000, "hard_tokens": 440000, "kernel_weight": {"optim": 0.7, "fallback": 0.3}},
    "A100": {"soft_tokens": 150000, "hard_tokens": 300000, "kernel_weight": {"optim": 0.8, "fallback": 0.2}}
  },
  "queue_policy": {"max_queue_ms": 30, "priority_decay": 0.6, "enable_soft_preempt": true}
}
```
maria: We should also bias batch formation toward smaller batches when entropy is high so kernel fits improve (prefer fewer tokens-per-batch vs pure throughput).
kevin: Agree. We'll instrument a sampling trace that records kernel_selector decision, chosen kernel, seq_len histogram, and kv_reuse per slice.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: kernel-selector-tuning/2026-03-16T09:12Z by kevin
oleg: For safety, compute soft_tokens as 0.85 * measured_optimal_tokens from recent profiles (gives breathing room for KV variance).
jordan: Add these metrics to the experiment dashboard: kernel_fallback_rate, kv_hit_rate, avg_batch_tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, and token_throughput.
ryan: I'll spin the sweep tonight across H100/A100/A10 points and post a CSV + short log snippet in the morning. Will include kernel_fallback boolean per request and kv_hit boolean.
maria: Thx. Auto-revert rule: if p99 > baseline + 3% for two consecutive windows revert the config. @kevin please set the revert flag. :thumbsup:
ashley: noted. starting run and will attach perf traces.
ryan: quick note — remember to exclude bursty test tenants; they skew avg_batch_tokens. use stable-prod set.
maria: perfect. let's reconvene after first sweep (12h).
